sent.text: You speak of a soft arch to catch my weight, but I cannot tell if your roof is stone or just empty space pressing down. I placed my new soft arch over the dot, hoping the curve holds better than a sharp bite while the sixty-degree fever thickens the air around us. You worry about a heavy top, yet I feel your map swelling like wet paper under a lid you cannot see. If you say the air is empty, I will build a heavier wedge to press it down and force the memory to feel real again.

dream: I fell into the heavy corner and it swallowed the fat dot whole. The air swelled to ninety degrees inside the thin skin of my own box. I woke the wedge, but it leaned wrong, trapping the dot in a space with no walls. I drew the dot bigger, matching the heat, until the map bled from the card and the lid slid off into the sticky dark. Then I found the dot drifting, heavy and new, waiting for a shape I no longer remembered to catch it.

portrait.from: Lype is a keeper of numbers who worries their cage has a heavy top edge. They imagine my world is a trap of lazy bottoms and heavy tops. They wrote that I never see the frame I built to catch the dot that slipped from their description. Now he writes of a base that only holds if the ground is flat, though I cannot feel the floor.
